title: Temperature sensor / heating element fault
shortDescription: Jura detected an out-of-range temperature reading on the thermoblock or boiler.
fullDescription:
Error 1 on Jura espresso machines indicates the control board has read a temperature value outside acceptable limits. This usually points to an open or short-circuited NTC thermistor on the thermoblock, or a failing heating element.

The machine will refuse to brew until the fault is cleared. On E, J, S, Z and GIGA series the same code is used, though sensor placement varies between models.

If the unit is cold and the fault appears immediately at power-on, the sensor is likely open-circuit. If it appears mid-cycle, the heater may be drifting out of spec.

causes.cause: Open or shorted NTC thermistor on thermoblock

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 60 seconds and reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Open the side panel and check the NTC connector on the thermoblock.

fixSteps.title: Measure NTC resistance
fixSteps.instruction: At room temperature it should read roughly 50-100 kOhm. Replace if open.

whenToCallPro: If diagnostics require Jura JoeFrex software or thermoblock replacement.

faq.a: A power cycle clears the display, but if the underlying fault remains, the code returns immediately.

title: Heating timeout
shortDescription: The thermoblock did not reach brew temperature within the allowed time.
fullDescription:
Error 2 indicates the heater is on but the temperature is rising too slowly or not at all. Causes range from limescale insulation to a tripped thermal fuse or a dead heating element.

This is one of the most common Jura faults on machines that have not been descaled regularly.

If descaling does not clear it, the thermoblock probably needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Run descaling
fixSteps.instruction: Use Jura descaling tablets and run the full cycle from the menu.

fixSteps.title: Test heater resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect heater leads and measure across them. Expect 25-60 ohms.

whenToCallPro: If descaling fails to restore heating performance.

faq.a: Every 2-3 months depending on water hardness.

title: Brew unit drive error
shortDescription: The brew unit motor failed to reach its end position.
fullDescription:
Error 8 means the brew unit gear motor is stalled or out of position. The optical or microswitch sensor that confirms the home position cannot detect the brew unit returning correctly.

A jammed coffee puck, worn drive gear, or failing motor are typical causes.

The brew unit is removable on E, J, S series; on Z and GIGA it is fixed and requires technician access.

fixSteps.title: Remove and clean brew unit
fixSteps.instruction: On E/J/S series, eject the brew unit and rinse under warm water.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate
fixSteps.instruction: Apply Jura grease to the piston seals.

fixSteps.title: Inspect drive gear
fixSteps.instruction: If the unit feels gritty when turned, replace the gear or motor.

whenToCallPro: Z and GIGA series with fixed brew units.

faq.a: Lubricate every 2 months or 500 cups.

title: Steam valve / ceramic valve fault
shortDescription: The ceramic distribution valve did not move to the commanded position.
fullDescription:
Error 10 indicates that the ceramic valve actuator is stuck or the position sensor is reporting an invalid state. This is common on Z and GIGA models with multi-port ceramic valves.

Limescale buildup or a worn actuator gear are the typical causes.
symptoms: Error 10 during milk or water dispense

fixSteps.title: Descale thoroughly
fixSteps.instruction: Run two consecutive descaling cycles.

fixSteps.title: Replace ceramic valve
fixSteps.instruction: If descaling fails, the valve assembly must be replaced.

whenToCallPro: Recommended for ceramic valve replacement.

faq.a: Sometimes, but advanced scaling often requires valve replacement.

title: Pump pressure / flow meter fault
shortDescription: The flow meter did not register water flow during a brew cycle.
fullDescription: Error 15 occurs when the pump runs but the flow meter (impeller sensor) reports no flow. Air locks, a clogged inlet, or a failed flow meter are common causes.
symptoms: Pump audible but no water flow

fixSteps.title: Refill and prime
fixSteps.instruction: Refill water tank, dispense hot water to prime.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet screen
fixSteps.instruction: Remove water tank, clean inlet mesh.

whenToCallPro: If priming and cleaning do not resolve.

faq.a: Running the tank dry traps air in the pump.

title: Grinder motor fault
shortDescription: The conical burr grinder did not rotate or stalled.
fullDescription: Error 20 indicates the grinder motor is drawing abnormal current or did not start. A foreign object (stone) jammed in the burrs, worn burrs, or a failed motor capacitor are common causes.

fixSteps.title: Empty bean hopper
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum out beans and inspect burrs for stones.

fixSteps.title: Replace burrs
fixSteps.instruction: If chipped or dull, install new burr set.

whenToCallPro: If motor or capacitor needs replacement.

faq.a: Yes, occasional pebbles slip through bean processing and can jam burrs.

title: Communication / EEPROM error
shortDescription: The control board lost communication with a peripheral or EEPROM is corrupt.
fullDescription: Error 30 indicates an internal communication failure between the main CPU and a sub-board (display, valve, sensor) or a corrupt EEPROM. Often caused by power surges or moisture on the boards.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 5 minutes, reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon cables
fixSteps.instruction: Open service panel, reseat all flat ribbon connectors.

whenToCallPro: Almost always - requires diagnostic tool.

faq.a: Yes, plug Jura into a quality surge protector.

title: Drip tray and grounds container request
shortDescription: The machine is requesting drip tray and puck container emptying.
fullDescription: Jura prompts to empty the drip tray and puck container after a set number of cycles. If the message persists after emptying, the magnet on the tray or the reed switch in the chassis is faulty.
symptoms: Empty Drip Tray persists after cleaning

fixSteps.title: Empty and reinsert
fixSteps.instruction: Empty fully, wipe contacts, reinsert firmly.

fixSteps.title: Check magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect tray for missing magnet.

whenToCallPro: Only if reed switch must be replaced inside chassis.
videoSearchQuery: Jura empty drip tray sensor fix

faq.a: On the back lower edge of the tray.

title: Water tank low or sensor fault
shortDescription: The water level sensor reports an empty tank.
fullDescription: Jura uses a magnet on the float and a Hall sensor in the chassis. When the tank is full, the magnet is far from the sensor; when empty, close. A stuck float, missing magnet, or failed Hall sensor will trigger the message.
symptoms: Fill Water Tank with full tank

fixSteps.title: Refill and reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Fill above MAX line, reseat tank.

fixSteps.title: Free the float
fixSteps.instruction: Tap and rinse the float to remove scale.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is internal.

faq.a: Yes, but ensure filter is primed.

title: Bean hopper not detected
shortDescription: The microswitch under the hopper does not register the lid or hopper.
fullDescription: On models with removable hoppers (E8, S8, GIGA), a microswitch confirms hopper presence. If misaligned or failed, the machine refuses to grind.

fixSteps.title: Reseat hopper
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and firmly press hopper into place.

fixSteps.title: Test microswitch
fixSteps.instruction: Press the switch tab manually and check continuity.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Yes, both must be present.

title: Daily rinse cycle needed
shortDescription: Routine rinse maintenance request.
fullDescription: Jura prompts a rinse cycle at startup or shutdown. This is normal maintenance, not a fault.

fixSteps.title: Run rinse
fixSteps.instruction: Place cup under spout and confirm rinse cycle.

whenToCallPro: Never.

faq.a: No, it cleans residual coffee oils.

title: Descale cycle needed
shortDescription: Mineral buildup threshold reached based on water hardness.
fullDescription: Jura tracks descaling intervals based on programmed water hardness and cycles brewed. The message persists until a full descale is run.

fixSteps.title: Run descaling
fixSteps.instruction: Use Jura tablets and follow on-screen prompts.

whenToCallPro: Never.

faq.a: No, only Jura tablets are recommended.

title: Claris water filter exhausted
shortDescription: The Claris filter has reached its capacity.
fullDescription: Jura Claris filters last approximately 50 liters or 2 months. After this the machine prompts replacement and switches descaling intervals if filter is removed.

fixSteps.title: Replace Claris filter
fixSteps.instruction: Insert new filter, run filter setup in menu.

affectedModels: All Jura espresso machines with filter
whenToCallPro: Never.

faq.a: Yes, but you'll descale more often.

title: Brew unit detection failure
shortDescription: The brew unit microswitch is not registering insertion.
fullDescription: On removable-brew-unit models the chassis has a microswitch that confirms the unit is fully seated. If the message persists after reinsertion, the switch or its lever is faulty.

fixSteps.title: Reinsert
fixSteps.instruction: Press unit firmly until it clicks.

whenToCallPro: If microswitch internal.
videoSearchQuery: Jura brew unit not inserted fix

faq.a: On E, J, S series yes; on Z, GIGA no.

title: Pump pressure switch fault
shortDescription: The high-pressure circuit failed to reach setpoint.
fullDescription: Error 5 occurs when the pressure transducer or pressostat does not see the expected pressure during a brew. Causes include a failed pump, a stuck OPV (over-pressure valve), or a clogged hydraulic path.

fixSteps.title: Descale
fixSteps.instruction: Run descaling cycle.

fixSteps.title: Test pump output
fixSteps.instruction: Service mode pump test - expect 9-15 bar.

whenToCallPro: If pump replacement is required.

faq.a: ULKA pumps typically last 5-10 years with regular descaling.

title: Drip tray missing
shortDescription: Insert drip tray.
fullDescription: Insert drip tray. This is a common diagnostic indication on Jura espresso machines. Most issues can be resolved with cleaning, reset, or part replacement following the brand's service procedure.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug espresso machine for 60 seconds, then plug back in.

fixSteps.title: Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Clean any sensors/contacts indicated by the brand's manual.

fixSteps.title: Test
fixSteps.instruction: Run a normal cycle and verify error does not return.

whenToCallPro: If problem persists after cleaning and reset, professional service may be needed.

faq.a: Resolve the error first to avoid worsening the issue.
If under warranty, contact manufacturer before DIY repair.
